description: The figure contains three side-by-side grouped bar charts illustrating model perplexity under different quantization bit-widths for two methods, “Uniform” and “Ours,” across datasets labeled (a) WikiText, (b) (title not readable in the image), and (c) C4. In each subplot, the horizontal axis shows the category “Quantization Bits” with four discrete tick labels ordered left-to-right as 3, 4, 8, and 16, and the vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” on a linear scale. In (a) WikiText, the y-axis spans roughly 0 to a little above 30 with ticks at about 5-unit intervals; for each bit setting there are two adjacent bars: a blue “Uniform” bar and an orange “Ours” bar, with approximate values of ~30 vs ~21.5 at 3 bits, ~27 vs ~19 at 4 bits, ~26.5 vs ~18.3 at 8 bits, and ~26.5 vs ~18.3 at 16 bits. In (b), the y-axis spans roughly 0 to a little above 400 with ticks at about 50-unit intervals; the grouped bars show approximately ~410 (Uniform, blue) vs ~245 (Ours, orange) at 3 bits, ~315 vs ~178 at 4 bits, ~298 vs ~182 at 8 bits, and ~298 vs ~182 at 16 bits. In (c) C4, the y-axis spans roughly 0 to a little above 30 with ticks at about 5-unit intervals; the grouped bars are approximately ~29 (Uniform) vs ~20.5 (Ours) at 3 bits, ~25 vs ~18.1 at 4 bits, ~24.5 vs ~17.7 at 8 bits, and ~24.5 vs ~17.7 at 16 bits. Each subplot includes a legend in the upper-left identifying the blue bars as “Uniform” and the orange bars as “Ours,” the bars are not stacked (they are paired side-by-side within each quantization-bit group), and there are no visible annotations or special highlighting beyond the consistent color coding.
